scope: Theorem 11.9 (Classification with prescribed basis maps) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 93. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each finite admissible shape L, at all sufficiently closed uniform levels µ, the following assertions hold. 1. If X, Y ∈ GL, an isomorphism e∅ : X∅ ≃ Y∅ and arbitrary bijections between the chosen nonroot pieces of X and Y extend to a system isomorphism X ≃ Y . In particular GL is categorical at these levels. 2. Suppose X → Y and X → Z are arrows in GL. Choose pieces of X, extend them to pieces of Y and Z, and prescribe a bijection CY s ≃ CZ s for every active label s. Then there is a system isomorphism Y ≃X Z realizing every prescribed bijection. The complementary cardinalities may be less than µ, and zero is allowed. The level requirements are uniform over the finitely many shapes at any fixed number of axes.
